subject: Seabright DPA and SCCs — execution questions & next actions
messages:
From: Emma Holt <emma.holt@seabright.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@seabright.com
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 09:22:00 +0000
Subject: Seabright DPA: initial redline and SCC questions

Hi Soojin,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency examples. Legal has taken an initial pass on the DPA and attached their redlined version (see attachment). A few high-level asks from our side before we get to signature: 

- Clarify processor/subprocessor role language: your marked up clause changes the controller/processor mapping for the analytics pipeline — we want explicit confirmation of which subprocessor(s) will see customer PII and for what purposes.
- SCCs: your draft references the EU SCCs (V4) but doesn’t include the signed annex; are you proposing RWI’s standard SCCs matrix as part of the exhibit?
- KMS / key custody: we need to know if keys can be customer-managed (bring-your-own-key) for EU customer data. If not, what encryption-at-rest responsibilities will you accept?

I’ve looped in procurement for contracting cadence. We can set a call if that helps.

Attachment: Seabright_DPA_redline_20261130.docx (docx)

Best,
Emma
Emma Holt
Head of Legal, Seabright Retail
emma.holt@seabright.com

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Holt <emma.holt@seabright.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Seabright DPA: initial redline and SCC questions

Emma — thanks for the redline and clear asks. Quick read-through and next steps below; attaching our consolidated redline and an SCCs matrix for reference.

Summary of RWI positions (short):
- Subprocessors: we will publish the subprocessor roster and commit to 30 days notice before adding any subprocessor that processes EU personal data. For analytics, the processors listed in Exhibit B will be the only ones with access to PII; we accept a contractual audit right limited to SOC2-type evidence and scoped to the service.
- SCCs: we use the EU Commission standard clauses v4 as baseline and provide an SCC matrix as an annex that maps roles and transfer pathways. We can include a signed annex at execution.
- KMS: we currently offer customer-managed keys for Dedicated and Private deployments only. For hosted (standard) deployments, keys are managed by Redwood; we’re willing to document key separation and per-customer envelope encryption, but cannot offer true BYOK for hosted in the initial contract.

Action items I propose: 
1) Internal legal sync (RWI): Ben & Laura — can you confirm if the analytics subprocessors list below is exhaustive for Seabright’s use case? Iren e, please confirm audit evidence scope wording.
2) Customer call: propose Wed 2026-12-02 14:00 UTC (30 minutes) to walk the redline and agree critical opens (subprocessors, KMS). Emma/procurement — can you confirm?
3) Deliverables: RWI to share SCCs matrix (attached) and a short Transfer Impact Summary by EOD Wed.

Attachments: RWI_SCCs_matrix.pdf; Seabright_DPA_redline_20261201.docx

Thanks,
Soojin
Soojin Lee
Director, Legal Ops — Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>, Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Dec 2026 12:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Seabright DPA: initial redline and SCC questions

Looping back on subprocessors: the analytics pipeline processors are (1) MetricStream Labs (analytics compute, US-hosted, SOC2), (2) KvCache Solutions (KV cache provider, EU & US), and (3) StorageLayer Inc. (object store, US, replicated to EU regions for DR).

Notes: 
- For Seabright’s expected volume, MetricStream will not see raw PII unless customer config enables payload-level logs; we can make that an opt-in telemetry setting.
- We agree to 30-day notice and SOC2 evidence; for more intrusive audits we’ll require a narrow scope and joint legal signoff.

Irene — can you confirm the exact language we should offer for the audit evidence (SOC2 + scoped inspection) so Soojin can feed into the call agenda?

Ben
Senior Contracts Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Dec 2026 08:40:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Seabright DPA: initial redline and SCC questions

Soojin / Ben — drafted suggested language snippets below we should propose on the call and include in a consolidated redline after alignment: 

1) Subprocessor notice / roster: "Redwood will maintain and publish a current list of subprocessors on its website and provide Customer with at least thirty (30) days’ advance notice prior to permitting any new subprocessor to process Personal Data. For any new subprocessor proposed to process Personal Data, Customer may object in writing within thirty (30) days of receipt of notice; any dispute will be escalated to designated signatories for resolution."

2) Audit evidence: "Customer shall be entitled to receive copies of Redwood’s SOC2 Type II report and summary of the scope of controls applicable to the Service. For any additional inspection or on-site audit request, Customer must provide a written justification and such audit shall be subject to agreed scope and reimbursable costs."

3) SCCs annex: include an annex that maps controller/processor responsibilities and lists transfers by logical subsystem (analytics, cache, storage). I recommend we attach the RWI_SCCs_matrix.pdf and an abbreviated Transfer Impact Summary to the order form as exhibits.

Irene — if you can confirm we are comfortable with the BYOK limitation language that will close the KMS ask for hosted deployments, we can mark that as a negotiation point rather than a blocker.

Laura
VP, Legal — Redwood Inference

Attachment: Seabright_Transfer_Impact_Summary.xlsx (xlsx, 12 KB)

From: Emma Holt <emma.holt@seabright.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: procurement@seabright.com, Alston Brown <alstonbrown@bclaw.com>
Date: Thu, 3 Dec 2026 16:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Seabright DPA: initial redline and SCC questions

Thanks — that write-up is helpful and the proposed wording looks reasonable as a starting point. Procurement confirms Wed 14:00 UTC works; we’ll treat the KMS limitation as a negotiation item, not an absolute blocker. A couple of final asks ahead of the call: 

- Could you share a 1-page data flow diagram focused on EU workloads (who processes what, and where)? That will help our privacy team assess transfer risk quickly.
- Please include the SCCs matrix and Transfer Impact Summary in the call materials (I see attachments in the thread, thanks).

We’ll have Alston (external counsel) on the call to advise on SCC annex language. DocuSign routing will be procurement-led after we agree on the final exhibits.

See you on Wed,
Emma
